actions.summary: Memory reliability and retention time are fundamentally limited by energy dissipation. Our revision incorporates findings that non-equilibrium environments and non-reciprocal couplings modulate Landauer erasure costs, establishing that predictive power in information engines is constrained by available energy and coarse-grained state access. Additionally, we contextualize these physical costs with operational overheads, where excessive data retention in cloud systems demonstrates a practical parallel to thermodynamic inefficiency, albeit driven by configuration rather than entropy bounds.
